subtopic: Geometrical Meaning of the Zeroes of a Polynomial
stem: Look at the graphs in Fig. 2.9 given below. Each is the graph of \(y = p(x)\), where \(p(x)\) is a polynomial. For each of the graphs, find the number of zeroes of \(p(x)\).
solution:
The zeroes of \(p(x)\) are exactly the \(x\)-coordinates of the points where the graph of \(y = p(x)\) meets the \(x\)-axis, so counting zeroes means counting those intersection points.

(i) The number of zeroes is 1 as the graph intersects the \(x\)-axis at one point only.
(ii) The number of zeroes is 2 as the graph intersects the \(x\)-axis at two points.
(iii) The number of zeroes is 3. (Why?)
(iv) The number of zeroes is 1. (Why?)
(v) The number of zeroes is 1. (Why?)
(vi) The number of zeroes is 4. (Why?)

subtopic: Zeroes and Coefficients of a Quadratic Polynomial
stem: Find the zeroes of the quadratic polynomial \(x^2 + 7x + 10\), and verify the relationship between the zeroes and the coefficients.
solution:
We have

\(x^2 + 7x + 10 = (x + 2)(x + 5)\)

So, the value of \(x^2 + 7x + 10\) is zero when \(x + 2 = 0\) or \(x + 5 = 0\), i.e., when \(x = -2\) or \(x = -5\). Therefore, the zeroes of \(x^2 + 7x + 10\) are \(-2\) and \(-5\). Now,

sum of zeroes \(= -2 + (-5) = -(7) = \dfrac{-(7)}{1} = \dfrac{-(\text{Coefficient of } x)}{\text{Coefficient of } x^2}\),

product of zeroes \(= (-2) \times (-5) = 10 = \dfrac{10}{1} = \dfrac{\text{Constant term}}{\text{Coefficient of } x^2}\).

subtopic: Zeroes and Coefficients of a Quadratic Polynomial
stem: Find the zeroes of the polynomial \(x^2 - 3\) and verify the relationship between the zeroes and the coefficients.
solution:
Recall the identity \(a^2 - b^2 = (a - b)(a + b)\). Using it, we can write:

\(x^2 - 3 = \left(x - \sqrt{3}\right)\left(x + \sqrt{3}\right)\)

So, the value of \(x^2 - 3\) is zero when \(x = \sqrt{3}\) or \(x = -\sqrt{3}\).

Therefore, the zeroes of \(x^2 - 3\) are \(\sqrt{3}\) and \(-\sqrt{3}\). Now,

sum of zeroes \(= \sqrt{3} - \sqrt{3} = 0 = \dfrac{-(\text{Coefficient of } x)}{\text{Coefficient of } x^2}\),

product of zeroes \(= \left(\sqrt{3}\right)\left(-\sqrt{3}\right) = -3 = \dfrac{-3}{1} = \dfrac{\text{Constant term}}{\text{Coefficient of } x^2}\).

subtopic: Forming a Quadratic Polynomial from its Zeroes
stem: Find a quadratic polynomial, the sum and product of whose zeroes are \(-3\) and \(2\), respectively.
solution:
Let the quadratic polynomial be \(ax^2 + bx + c\), and its zeroes be \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\). We have

\(\alpha + \beta = -3 = \dfrac{-b}{a}\),

and \(\alpha\beta = 2 = \dfrac{c}{a}\).

If \(a = 1\), then \(b = 3\) and \(c = 2\).

So, one quadratic polynomial which fits the given conditions is \(x^2 + 3x + 2\).

You can check that any other quadratic polynomial that fits these conditions will be of the form \(k(x^2 + 3x + 2)\), where \(k\) is real.

subtopic: Zeroes and Coefficients of a Quadratic Polynomial
stem: Verify that \(3,\ -1,\ -\dfrac{1}{3}\) are the zeroes of the cubic polynomial \(p(x) = 3x^3 - 5x^2 - 11x - 3\), and then verify the relationship between the zeroes and the coefficients.
solution:
Comparing the given polynomial with \(ax^3 + bx^2 + cx + d\), we get \(a = 3\), \(b = -5\), \(c = -11\), \(d = -3\). Further,

\(p(3) = 3 \times 3^3 - (5 \times 3^2) - (11 \times 3) - 3 = 81 - 45 - 33 - 3 = 0\),

\(p(-1) = 3 \times (-1)^3 - 5 \times (-1)^2 - 11 \times (-1) - 3 = -3 - 5 + 11 - 3 = 0\),

\(p\left(-\dfrac{1}{3}\right) = 3 \times \left(-\dfrac{1}{3}\right)^3 - 5 \times \left(-\dfrac{1}{3}\right)^2 - 11 \times \left(-\dfrac{1}{3}\right) - 3 = -\dfrac{1}{9} - \dfrac{5}{9} + \dfrac{11}{3} - 3 = -\dfrac{2}{3} + \dfrac{2}{3} = 0\).

Therefore, \(3\), \(-1\) and \(-\dfrac{1}{3}\) are the zeroes of \(3x^3 - 5x^2 - 11x - 3\).

So, we take \(\alpha = 3\), \(\beta = -1\) and \(\gamma = -\dfrac{1}{3}\). Now,

\(\alpha + \beta + \gamma = 3 + (-1) + \left(-\dfrac{1}{3}\right) = 2 - \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{5}{3} = \dfrac{-(-5)}{3} = \dfrac{-b}{a}\),

\(\alpha\beta + \beta\gamma + \gamma\alpha = 3 \times (-1) + (-1) \times \left(-\dfrac{1}{3}\right) + \left(-\dfrac{1}{3}\right) \times 3 = -3 + \dfrac{1}{3} - 1 = \dfrac{-11}{3} = \dfrac{c}{a}\),

\(\alpha\beta\gamma = 3 \times (-1) \times \left(-\dfrac{1}{3}\right) = 1 = \dfrac{-(-3)}{3} = \dfrac{-d}{a}\).

Note: the textbook marks this example with an asterisk, "Not from the examination point of view."

subtopic: Geometrical Meaning of the Zeroes of a Polynomial
stem: The graphs of \(y = p(x)\) are given in Fig. 2.10 below, for some polynomials \(p(x)\). Find the number of zeroes of \(p(x)\), in each case.
solution:
A zero of \(p(x)\) is an \(x\)-coordinate at which the graph of \(y = p(x)\) cuts or touches the \(x\)-axis, so read off the number of such points in each graph.

(i) No zeroes, since the graph is a line lying entirely above the \(x\)-axis and never meets it.
(ii) 1, since the graph crosses the \(x\)-axis at exactly one point.
(iii) 3, since the graph crosses the \(x\)-axis at three points.
(iv) 2, since the graph crosses the \(x\)-axis at two points.
(v) 4, since the graph crosses the \(x\)-axis at four points.
(vi) 3, since the graph crosses the \(x\)-axis at three points.

subtopic: Zeroes and Coefficients of a Quadratic Polynomial
context: Find the zeroes of the following quadratic polynomials and verify the relationship between the zeroes and the coefficients.
solution:
\(x^2 - 2x - 8 = x^2 - 4x + 2x - 8 = x(x - 4) + 2(x - 4) = (x - 4)(x + 2)\)

So the zeroes are \(x = 4\) and \(x = -2\).

Here \(a = 1,\ b = -2,\ c = -8\).

Sum of zeroes \(= 4 + (-2) = 2 = \dfrac{-(-2)}{1} = \dfrac{-b}{a}\).

Product of zeroes \(= 4 \times (-2) = -8 = \dfrac{-8}{1} = \dfrac{c}{a}\).

subtopic: Zeroes and Coefficients of a Quadratic Polynomial
context: Find the zeroes of the following quadratic polynomials and verify the relationship between the zeroes and the coefficients.
solution:
\(4s^2 - 4s + 1 = (2s)^2 - 2(2s)(1) + 1^2 = (2s - 1)^2\)

So \(2s - 1 = 0\) twice, giving the repeated zero \(s = \dfrac{1}{2}\).

Here \(a = 4,\ b = -4,\ c = 1\).

Sum of zeroes \(= \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} = 1 = \dfrac{-(-4)}{4} = \dfrac{-b}{a}\).

Product of zeroes \(= \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{1}{4} = \dfrac{c}{a}\).

subtopic: Zeroes and Coefficients of a Quadratic Polynomial
context: Find the zeroes of the following quadratic polynomials and verify the relationship between the zeroes and the coefficients.
solution:
Write it in standard form: \(6x^2 - 7x - 3\). Split the middle term using \(6 \times (-3) = -18 = (-9) \times 2\):

\(6x^2 - 7x - 3 = 6x^2 - 9x + 2x - 3 = 3x(2x - 3) + 1(2x - 3) = (3x + 1)(2x - 3)\)

So the zeroes are \(x = -\dfrac{1}{3}\) and \(x = \dfrac{3}{2}\).

Here \(a = 6,\ b = -7,\ c = -3\).

Sum of zeroes \(= -\dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{3}{2} = \dfrac{-2 + 9}{6} = \dfrac{7}{6} = \dfrac{-(-7)}{6} = \dfrac{-b}{a}\).

Product of zeroes \(= \left(-\dfrac{1}{3}\right) \times \dfrac{3}{2} = -\dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{-3}{6} = \dfrac{c}{a}\).

subtopic: Zeroes and Coefficients of a Quadratic Polynomial
context: Find the zeroes of the following quadratic polynomials and verify the relationship between the zeroes and the coefficients.
solution:
\(4u^2 + 8u = 4u(u + 2)\)

So the zeroes are \(u = 0\) and \(u = -2\).

Here \(a = 4,\ b = 8,\ c = 0\).

Sum of zeroes \(= 0 + (-2) = -2 = \dfrac{-8}{4} = \dfrac{-b}{a}\).

Product of zeroes \(= 0 \times (-2) = 0 = \dfrac{0}{4} = \dfrac{c}{a}\).

subtopic: Zeroes and Coefficients of a Quadratic Polynomial
context: Find the zeroes of the following quadratic polynomials and verify the relationship between the zeroes and the coefficients.
solution:
\(t^2 - 15 = \left(t - \sqrt{15}\right)\left(t + \sqrt{15}\right)\)

So the zeroes are \(t = \sqrt{15}\) and \(t = -\sqrt{15}\).

Here \(a = 1,\ b = 0,\ c = -15\).

Sum of zeroes \(= \sqrt{15} + \left(-\sqrt{15}\right) = 0 = \dfrac{-0}{1} = \dfrac{-b}{a}\).

Product of zeroes \(= \sqrt{15} \times \left(-\sqrt{15}\right) = -15 = \dfrac{-15}{1} = \dfrac{c}{a}\).

subtopic: Zeroes and Coefficients of a Quadratic Polynomial
context: Find the zeroes of the following quadratic polynomials and verify the relationship between the zeroes and the coefficients.
solution:
Split the middle term using \(3 \times (-4) = -12 = (-4) \times 3\):

\(3x^2 - x - 4 = 3x^2 - 4x + 3x - 4 = x(3x - 4) + 1(3x - 4) = (3x - 4)(x + 1)\)

So the zeroes are \(x = \dfrac{4}{3}\) and \(x = -1\).

Here \(a = 3,\ b = -1,\ c = -4\).

Sum of zeroes \(= \dfrac{4}{3} + (-1) = \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{-(-1)}{3} = \dfrac{-b}{a}\).

Product of zeroes \(= \dfrac{4}{3} \times (-1) = -\dfrac{4}{3} = \dfrac{-4}{3} = \dfrac{c}{a}\).

subtopic: Forming a Quadratic Polynomial from its Zeroes
context: Find a quadratic polynomial each with the given numbers as the sum and product of its zeroes respectively.
solution:
A quadratic polynomial whose zeroes have sum \(S\) and product \(P\) is \(k\left(x^2 - Sx + P\right)\), for any non-zero real \(k\).

Here \(S = \dfrac{1}{4}\) and \(P = -1\), so the polynomial is \(k\left(x^2 - \dfrac{1}{4}x - 1\right)\).

Taking \(k = 4\) to clear the fraction gives \(4x^2 - x - 4\).

subtopic: Forming a Quadratic Polynomial from its Zeroes
context: Find a quadratic polynomial each with the given numbers as the sum and product of its zeroes respectively.
solution:
Here \(S = \sqrt{2}\) and \(P = \dfrac{1}{3}\), so the polynomial is \(k\left(x^2 - \sqrt{2}\,x + \dfrac{1}{3}\right)\).

Taking \(k = 3\) to clear the fraction gives \(3x^2 - 3\sqrt{2}\,x + 1\).

subtopic: Forming a Quadratic Polynomial from its Zeroes
context: Find a quadratic polynomial each with the given numbers as the sum and product of its zeroes respectively.
solution:
Here \(S = 0\) and \(P = \sqrt{5}\), so the polynomial is \(k\left(x^2 - 0 \cdot x + \sqrt{5}\right)\).

Taking \(k = 1\) gives \(x^2 + \sqrt{5}\).

subtopic: Forming a Quadratic Polynomial from its Zeroes
context: Find a quadratic polynomial each with the given numbers as the sum and product of its zeroes respectively.
solution:
Here \(S = 1\) and \(P = 1\), so the polynomial is \(k\left(x^2 - x + 1\right)\).

Taking \(k = 1\) gives \(x^2 - x + 1\).

subtopic: Forming a Quadratic Polynomial from its Zeroes
context: Find a quadratic polynomial each with the given numbers as the sum and product of its zeroes respectively.
solution:
Here \(S = -\dfrac{1}{4}\) and \(P = \dfrac{1}{4}\), so the polynomial is \(k\left(x^2 + \dfrac{1}{4}x + \dfrac{1}{4}\right)\).

Taking \(k = 4\) to clear the fractions gives \(4x^2 + x + 1\).

subtopic: Forming a Quadratic Polynomial from its Zeroes
context: Find a quadratic polynomial each with the given numbers as the sum and product of its zeroes respectively.
solution:
Here \(S = 4\) and \(P = 1\), so the polynomial is \(k\left(x^2 - 4x + 1\right)\).

Taking \(k = 1\) gives \(x^2 - 4x + 1\).
